solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Igor trained on piano, a Russian speciality (5)

indicators.note: Igor is put through training, so reshaped
in an across answer, one piece going on another sits after it

annotation.surface: A Russian named Igor, trained at the piano, is presented as a national speciality.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants the speciality to be a pianist; it is food instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A pirog is a traditional Russian baked pie, a speciality of that cuisine.

entries.clue: Oxford college set up member in Strasbourg out of funds (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means written upwards, so turned round

blocks.note: a Member of the European Parliament, which sits in Strasbourg

annotation.surface: An Oxford college has set up a European politician who has run out of money.
annotation.walkthrough: MEP is Member of the European Parliament; Strasbourg is one of its seats, so the city stands in for the institution.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Oxford, and Cambridge has one of the same name.

entries.clue: What’s left except for a souvenir? (8)

indicators.note: everything bar the A, so the A is taken out

blocks.note: the remainder is what is left over

annotation.surface: A wry question: is a souvenir all you have left after the holiday?
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the rueful joke that a souvenir is all that remains of the holiday.
annotation.definitionFit: A souvenir is kept to bring back memories of a place, which is exactly what a reminder does.

entries.clue: Long story forgotten, including its twist? (4,4,3,4)

blocks.note: its = the, the definite article standing for the possessive

annotation.surface: A long tale is forgotten, twist ending and all.
annotation.walkthrough: WIND must be read as the verb that rhymes with find, not the breeze. Margaret Mitchell's novel runs to over a thousand pages, hence 'Long story'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Margaret Mitchell's Civil War novel is famously long, over a thousand pages, and its film nearly four hours.

entries.clue: Periodically green couple use less energy after 1/12 (9)

indicators.note: use less energy: USE without its E
the rest follows the date

blocks.note: 1/12 in British date order is 1 December, written Dec I

annotation.surface: A tip about a couple going green by cutting energy use from the start of December.
annotation.walkthrough: The fraction 1/12 looks like arithmetic but is a date: Britain writes day then month, so 1/12 is the first of December, DEC plus the Roman I.
annotation.definitionFit: Deciduous trees are green only part of the year, shedding leaves each autumn.

entries.clue: Platform helps with AI being delayed (4)

indicators.note: the AI comes later than it should, moving from before the D to after it

blocks.note: read as the two letters A and I, not artificial intelligence; within AIDS they are the ones that shift later

annotation.surface: A platform company says its help will come with AI features, which are running late.
annotation.walkthrough: AI in the surface is artificial intelligence; in the wordplay it is just two letters, moved one place later in AIDS.
annotation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform for speakers or dignitaries.

entries.clue: Prisoner thought the experience was hell! (8,2)

blocks.note: 'found it hell' = thought the experience was hell

annotation.surface: An inmate reports that his time inside was hell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hell' does double duty: it completes the prisoner's verdict (found it hell) and alone is the exclamation the answer means.
annotation.definitionFit: Both 'Hell!' and 'Confound it!' are mild oaths of annoyance.

entries.clue: Getting free delighted fish in dark twisted net (15)

indicators.note: SENT and ANGLE go inside DIM
a twisted thing is bent out of shape, so NET's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
NET rearranged, placed after the container

annotation.surface: Someone happily frees a fish caught in a tangled net in the dark.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fish' is the verb, not a creature swimming in the net; and 'delighted' is the old slang sense of sent, thrilled.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in noun form: the process of getting free, whether from a net or a messy situation.

entries.clue: Staff shop for booze which Charlie cracks open (6)

indicators.note: C breaks into the word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: an offie is an off-licence, a British liquor store
surface padding, joining the shop to what happens to it
C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: At the liquor store, someone named Charlie cracks open a bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: An offie is British slang for an off-licence, a shop selling alcohol to take away.
annotation.definitionFit: The office can mean the staff who work there collectively.

entries.clue: Ice starts to trouble experienced brothers on the climb (6)

indicators.note: the start of each word is what is taken, here the opening letters of trouble and experienced
in a down answer, climbing means reading upward

blocks.note: first letters of trouble and experienced

annotation.surface: A mountaineering scene: ice causes early problems for climbing brothers.
annotation.walkthrough: The climbing brothers belong to the surface; the ice they meet on the mountain is the dessert.
annotation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a water ice, a frozen dessert.

entries.clue: Large tasteless house from 1900 redeveloped as “old” inn (9)

indicators.note: the letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A big ugly house built after 1900 has been done up as a mock-old inn.
annotation.walkthrough: O is the standard abbreviation for old.
annotation.definitionFit: McMansion is a derogatory term for a large, tastelessly built modern house.

entries.clue: Bed for homeless surfer? Right, up to a point (2,3)

blocks.note: a sofa-surfer sleeps on friends' sofas

annotation.surface: Someone asks where a homeless sofa-surfer sleeps, and gets a grudging 'right, up to a point'.
annotation.walkthrough: A sofa-surfer or couch-surfer is someone without a home who sleeps on friends' sofas; the question mark flags that this bed is described cryptically.
annotation.definitionFit: 'So far' means to a limited extent, up to a point, as in 'I trust him only so far'.

entries.clue: Celebrity touching this minute kitten’s tail (6)

indicators.note: the last letter of kitten

annotation.surface: A celebrity touching a kitten's tail right now, as in a viral photo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Celebrity' is the abstract noun, fame, not a famous person.
annotation.definitionFit: Celebrity in its older abstract sense, the state of being famous rather than a famous person, is a plain synonym here.

entries.clue: Coastal road that’s lovely, with a small market (8)

blocks.note: cor! is a British exclamation of admiration
a niche market is a small specialised one

annotation.surface: A travel blurb praising a lovely coastal road with a little market along it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' is a British working-class exclamation, roughly 'wow', so it can stand for 'that's lovely!'.
annotation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut into a cliff along a coast.

entries.clue: Small planet full of holes dug for extracting slime (10)

indicators.note: the planet is filled with the holes, so contains them

blocks.note: the red planet, the outer part
mines are holes dug to extract minerals

annotation.surface: A small planet riddled with mining holes is being used to extract slime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slime' is the figurative sense, oily ingratiation, and sits at the end looking like the thing being extracted.
annotation.definitionFit: Slime, in the sense of oily flattery, is smarminess.

entries.clue: Taking nut, fix IKEA lamp to cabin’s exterior (12)

indicators.note: the letters are fixed up into a new order
only the outside letters of cabin

blocks.note: outer letters of cabin, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Flat-pack instructions: take a nut and fix the IKEA lamp to the outside of the cabin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking nut' looks like an instruction from the assembly leaflet; read it as one noun phrase, a nut (crazy person) who takes things.
annotation.definitionFit: A kleptomaniac compulsively steals, so is a nut for taking things.

entries.clue: Settle report of explosion you heard recently (8)

indicators.note: what is heard is a sound, so we take the letter that sounds like 'you'

blocks.note: a pop is the sound of a small explosion

annotation.surface: A news report asks whether you heard the explosion recently, and to settle the matter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Report' here is the bang itself, not a news story. 'Settle' is the verb meaning to colonise.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the colonising sense: to settle a territory is to fill it with inhabitants.

entries.clue: Homeless shelters buy up military art (8)

indicators.note: STRAY holds TEG inside it
in a down answer, up means written upwards, so turned round

blocks.note: a stray has no home; the outer part

annotation.surface: Homeless shelters buying up military art as an investment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Homeless shelters' reads as a noun phrase, but Homeless is the stray and shelters is the verb doing the containing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the Greek strategia, generalship: the discipline of planning a war.

entries.clue: Course’s marker showing skill in smart job (8,4)

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so ART goes within STING

blocks.note: to smart is to sting; the outer part

annotation.surface: A golf-course marker shows how skilful someone was at a smart job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smart' is the verb, to sting, not the adjective meaning clever or well dressed. The course is a racecourse.
annotation.definitionFit: The starting post marks where a race begins on a racecourse.

entries.clue: Be careful with bread sons pinch into shape (6)

blocks.note: to crimp is to pinch edges into folds, as on a pie

annotation.surface: Baking advice: careful with the dough, sons, pinch it into shape.
annotation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so being careful with bread is being thrifty; the surface wants it to be the loaf.
annotation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be very economical with money.

entries.clue: Sexy character’s promises likely to come to nothing (3,3)

definitions.text: promises likely to come to nothing

blocks.note: an air is a manner or character; the 's is 'is', joining the parts

annotation.surface: A seductive charmer's promises are unlikely to be kept.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's after character is 'is', gluing the wordplay to the definition, rather than a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: empty talk, the kind of big promise that evaporates like warm air.

entries.clue: Almost right, racket shortened as mid-winter approaches? (6,2)

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise

annotation.surface: A near-miss racket cut short as winter comes on, like a tennis season ending.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Racket shortened' looks like a deletion instruction, but 'shortened' belongs to the definition: the days have closed in.
annotation.definitionFit: Days are said to close in, becoming shorter, as midwinter approaches.

entries.clue: Petrifying woman alarmed US Airbnb hosts (6)

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, as a host has guests

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of alarmed, all of US, and the start of Airbnb

annotation.surface: A terrifying woman scared the Americans who were hosting her through Airbnb.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Petrifying' is literal: this woman turned people to stone.
annotation.definitionFit: Medusa, the Gorgon of Greek myth, turned anyone who looked at her to stone.

entries.clue: Sound from butchered birds is horrible (4)

indicators.note: what we need is how the word sounds

blocks.note: fowl are birds, especially poultry for the table

annotation.surface: The noise from slaughtered birds is horrible.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butchered' tells you the birds are poultry, the kind called fowl.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word covers anything offensive or nasty, just as horrible does.

entries.clue: Two eating butter sent back fine Japanese dishes (5)

indicators.note: what eats something takes it inside, so II swallows MAR
something sent back goes the way it came, so RAM is read right to left

blocks.note: 2 in Roman numerals; the outer part
a ram butts with its head

annotation.surface: Two diners eating butter send back their fine Japanese dishes.
annotation.walkthrough: A butter is 'one who butts', so a ram, not the dairy spread. Dishes are the porcelain itself, not food.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a Japanese porcelain named after its export port, prized for plates and bowls.

entries.clue: Without any price, free of charge (9)

blocks.note: ex = without, as in ex dividend

annotation.surface: Something offered without any price is free of charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Free of charge' means without cost in the surface; as a definition it means clear of an accusation.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: 'charge' is an accusation, and the verb means to clear a person of one.

entries.clue: Heavenly secretary tormented sad liar (9)

indicators.note: the letters are twisted about

annotation.surface: A divine secretary tormented a miserable liar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly secretary' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: Paradisal means of or like paradise, heavenly.

entries.clue: Shirt without buttons nursery cleared out is extra small (5)

indicators.note: the middle of nursery is emptied, leaving its ends

annotation.surface: A buttonless shirt the nursery has cleared out is in size extra small.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extra small' looks like a clothing size on the label; here it is just the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal, childlike synonym: baby talk for tiny, a fit for the nursery in the surface.
